# Network-analysis conformance fixtures

Every binary in this directory is generated by
[`generate-fixtures.mjs`](generate-fixtures.mjs). The corpus contains no
captured user, production, runner, or third-party traffic. It uses RFC 5737
documentation addresses, reserved example domains, and obvious synthetic
secret/PII canaries. The generator and outputs are distributed under the
repository's MIT license.

Run the generator and verify there is no drift:

```bash
node test/fixtures/network-analysis/generate-fixtures.mjs
git diff --exit-code -- test/fixtures/network-analysis
```

[`manifest.v1.json`](manifest.v1.json) records byte sizes, SHA-256 hashes,
expected traffic, origin, license, and sensitivity. The largest binary is under
256 bytes. [`conformance-report.v1.json`](conformance-report.v1.json) is the
machine-readable release receipt and documents recipe, adapter, negative-case,
redaction, and supported-version coverage.

The default conformance suite uses mocks/stubs and never opens an interface.
An installed TShark can be checked only against `synthetic-dns.pcap`:

```bash
AIWG_NETWORK_ANALYSIS_LIVE=1 \
AIWG_NETWORK_ANALYSIS_TSHARK=/absolute/path/to/tshark \
npx vitest run --config config/vitest.conformance.config.js \
  test/conformance/network-analysis-v1/network-analysis.test.ts
```

This opt-in check reads a saved synthetic capture. It does not run dumpcap,
tcpdump, active scanning, or live capture. Termshark conformance always uses a
noninteractive executable stub in `test/unit/network-analysis/termshark.test.ts`.
